question.text: Vindhya Venture Fund (Category I VC) faces a temporary liquidity gap when an investor delays paying the capital call on an imminent Series B round. What borrowing flexibility is available to this Cat I AIF at fund level?

answer.text: Up to 2x of investable funds, consistent with Cat III leverage norms
Unlimited borrowing as long as the delaying investor is charged the cost
Borrowing of up to 10% of investable funds, for a maximum of 30 days, not more than 4 occasions a year, with a 30-day cooling-off between borrowings
Borrowing permitted only against earmarked Government securities with zero interest charge

explanation.text: The Logic: Category I and II AIFs are prohibited from fund-level leverage EXCEPT to meet temporary funding requirements: up to 10% of investable funds, for not more than 30 days, on not more than 4 occasions a year, with a 30-day cooling-off period between borrowings. Additionally, SEBI Circular of Aug 19, 2024 permits short-term borrowing for drawdown shortfalls (cost charged only to delaying investor). The Trap: Option A is the Cat III 2x leverage cap — does NOT apply to Cat I/II (classic trap). Option B ignores the percentage/frequency limits. Option D describes CDS earmarking mechanics, not general borrowing. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-E cover Cat III 2x leverage (calculation, reporting). XIX-D (this exam) excludes Cat III leverage as primary subject matter. XIX-A Distributors should know the Cat I/II borrowing floor so they can explain PPM language on 'temporary liquidity facility' to HNI clients. Manager's Pro-Tip: The 30-day cooling-off is a common operational trip-wire. Build a treasury calendar mapping each borrowing window and schedule capital calls 45 days before any large commitment to avoid back-to-back emergency draws. Disclose the borrowing policy clearly in PPM Section 'Fund Borrowings'.
